clinician.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old Caucasian girl with primary hypoparathyroidism diagnosed at age 9 presented with seizures and syncope, found to have hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and low PTH (E001), with bilateral basal ganglia and frontal lobe calcifications on CT/MR imaging (E002). She was initiated on calcium supplementation and 1-α-hydroxycholecalciferol at age 9. In January 2015 (age 14), she experienced a severe hypercalcemic crisis presenting with dyspnea, generalized weakness, polydipsia, nausea, and tachycardia, requiring hospitalization with intensive fluid therapy, loop diuretics, and temporary withdrawal of vitamin D and calcium (E003). By September 2015, she was admitted to the Department of Pediatric Nephrology with nephrocalcinosis and difficulty achieving normocalcemia. At this admission, biochemical testing revealed persistent hypoparathyroidism (low PTH, low 25-OH-vitamin D, low alkaline phosphatase, hyperphosphatemia, and decreased total and ionized calcium) (E005), persistent hypercalciuria (calcium-to-creatinine ratio 0.24 mg/mg with decreased magnesium-to-calcium ratio of 0.25 mg/mg) (E005), and normal renal function (eGFR 92 ml/min/1.73 m²) (E005). Imaging revealed mild nephrocalcinosis with increased echogenicity of the renal pyramid borders (E004). The nephrocalcinosis represents a complication of chronic dysregulation of mineral metabolism and persistent hypercalciuria despite 5 years of calcium and calcitriol therapy.

final.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old Caucasian girl with primary hypoparathyroidism diagnosed at age 9 presented with seizures and syncope, found to have hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and low PTH (E001), with bilateral basal ganglia and frontal lobe calcifications on CT/MR imaging (E002). She was initiated on calcium supplementation and 1-α-hydroxycholecalciferol at age 9. In January 2015 (age 14), she experienced a severe hypercalcemic crisis presenting with dyspnea, generalized weakness, polydipsia, nausea, and tachycardia, requiring hospitalization with intensive fluid therapy, loop diuretics, and temporary withdrawal of vitamin D and calcium (E003). By September 2015, she was admitted to the Department of Pediatric Nephrology with nephrocalcinosis and difficulty achieving normocalcemia. At this admission, biochemical testing revealed persistent hypoparathyroidism (low PTH, low 25-OH-vitamin D, low alkaline phosphatase, hyperphosphatemia, and decreased total and ionized calcium) (E005), persistent hypercalciuria (calcium-to-creatinine ratio 0.24 mg/mg with decreased magnesium-to-calcium ratio of 0.25 mg/mg) (E005), and normal renal function (eGFR 92 ml/min/1.73 m²) (E005). Imaging revealed mild nephrocalcinosis with increased echogenicity of the renal pyramid borders (E004). The nephrocalcinosis represents a complication of chronic dysregulation of mineral metabolism and persistent hypercalciuria despite 5 years of calcium and calcitriol therapy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Primary hypoparathyroidism diagnosed at age 9 with characteristic biochemical abnormalities
Initial presentation at age 9 with seizures and syncope associated with intracranial calcifications (basal ganglia and frontal lobes)
Severe hypercalcemic crisis in January 2015 requiring hospitalization with symptoms of dyspnea, weakness, polydipsia, nausea, and tachycardia
